hints: Look at how atomic radius changes across Period 3, remembering that increasing nuclear charge pulls the outer electrons in closer.
D must be chlorine, the smallest atom in Period 3 when argon is compared by a different type of radius, now think about melting point order to find E.
List Period 3 melting points from lowest up, find the element with exactly two elements below it, then check which pair of elements can combine to give one of the listed formulas.
walkthrough:
**Identify element D from atomic radius**

Think across Period 3 from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Ar}$. Proton number increases, so nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar.

This pulls the outer shell closer, so atomic radius decreases across the period. The smallest covalent radius is chlorine, $\text{Cl}$. So D is $\text{Cl}$.

**Identify element E from melting points**

Recall the Period 3 melting point pattern. It rises from $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Si}$ (giant covalent, highest), then falls sharply to $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$, $\text{Cl}$, $\text{Ar}$ (simple molecular).

In order from lowest: $\text{Ar}$ < $\text{Cl}$ < $\text{P}$ < $\text{Na}$ < $\text{S}$ < $\text{Mg}$ < $\text{Al}$ < $\text{Si}$. Only two elements are lower than phosphorus, so E is $\text{P}$.

**Combine D and E to find L**

We have D = $\text{Cl}$ and E = $\text{P}$. These two non-metals react directly to form a covalent chloride of phosphorus.

$$\text{P} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{PCl}_3$$
This matches one of the options, so that must be compound L.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{MgCl}_2$ needs magnesium and chlorine. Chlorine is D, but magnesium is not E. Magnesium has a very high melting point with five elements below it, not two.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{MgS}$ needs magnesium and sulfur. Neither is D (chlorine) nor E (phosphorus). This is a trap if you guess common Period 3 ionic compounds without checking the trends.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$ needs sodium and sulfur. Sodium has three elements with lower melting points ($\text{Ar}$, $\text{Cl}$, $\text{P}$), not two, so it cannot be E.
options.D: Correct. D is $\text{Cl}$ (smallest atomic radius) and E is $\text{P}$ (third lowest melting point, only $\text{Ar}$ and $\text{Cl}$ are lower). Phosphorus and chlorine react to give $\text{PCl}_3$, so this is a possible compound L.
